mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT continue rising from their current lows, weekday foot traffic should recover and lift RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks. The mechanism fails if commuting activity stalls while retail remains near current levels or weakens.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved from -38.6 to -24.9 and TRANSIT from -51.9 to -37.0 across the snapshot window
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise above its last-4-week mean even though WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both improve for at least two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A continued rise in RESIDENTIAL mobility indicates more time spent at home, which suppresses discretionary shopping trips and pushes RETAIL_REC lower within two weeks. The claim fails if residential time stops increasing or retail recovers despite higher home stay.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL remained above baseline at 20.7, 16.7, 13.7, and 13.6 in the snapshot
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC is not lower than its last-4-week mean within 14 days while RESIDENTIAL stays above baseline.

mechanism_narrative: Once TRANSIT and WORKPLACES move back toward less-negative territory by at least 10 points from their current week, retail visitation should increase over the next four weeks because commuting-linked errands resume. The effect fails if mobility recovery is driven only by parks or home activity instead of commuting.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises above -30 and WORKPLACES rises above -20 week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT and WORKPLACES are still deeply negative at -37.0 and -24.9
failure_condition: After TRANSIT exceeds -30 and WORKPLACES exceeds -20, RETAIL_REC fails to improve over the following 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in PARKS mobility above its recent trough should precede a short-run lift in RETAIL_REC over the next week because leisure outings spill over into nearby shopping and dining. The hypothesis fails if park activity rises without any retail response.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises by at least 5 points from its current week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS improved to -6.4 before dropping to -24.1 in the latest week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase within 7 days after PARKS rises by at least 5 points from the prior week.

mechanism_narrative: If GROCERY_PHARM remains near baseline while WORKPLACES and TRANSIT stay depressed, consumers are still making only essential trips and retail discretionary spending stays weak over four weeks. The claim fails if essential mobility strengthens alongside discretionary retail.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM is close to zero while WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remain far below baseline
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its last-4-week mean while GROCERY_PHARM stays near zero and both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remain below -20.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained recovery in PARKS together with a continued easing in TRANSIT should raise weekend shopping and recreation demand, pushing RETAIL_REC upward over two weeks. The mechanism fails if outdoor activity recovers but transit use remains flat or retail does not follow.
candidate_trigger: PARKS turns positive week-on-week and TRANSIT improves by at least 5 points
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS and TRANSIT both weakened sharply in the latest week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not improve within 14 days after PARKS rises and TRANSIT improves by at least 5 points.

mechanism_narrative: A fall in RESIDENTIAL from its elevated level should free time for shopping trips and raise RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks. The claim fails if residence time stays elevated or retail remains stuck below the prior 4-week mean.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL has already eased from 20.7 to 13.6 but remains above baseline
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not exceed its last-4-week mean within 28 days after RESIDENTIAL falls below 12.

mechanism_narrative: When WORKPLACES and TRANSIT keep improving while PARKS stays depressed, the mobility mix shifts toward routine urban errands rather than leisure, which should lift RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks. The hypothesis fails if parks rebound first or commuting mobility deteriorates again.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES and TRANSIT are recovering more steadily than PARKS in the snapshot
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains below its last-4-week mean even though WORKPLACES and TRANSIT keep improving while PARKS stays at or below -20.
